summary:
THREE FINDINGS DOMINATE.

(1) THE DECISIVE QUESTION HAS ALREADY BEEN ANSWERED EMPIRICALLY, AND THE ANSWER WAS NO. corpus/eval/ does not exist and scripts/eval-retrieval.ts was never written -- both verified absent. But a working harness DOES exist, referenced by none of the four plans, at tmp/analysis-upgrade/production-sandbox/: a SHA-frozen 6-prompt suite (data/prompts/canonical-suite.json, sha256 recorded in ARTIFACT-MANIFEST.json, "FROZEN -- must not be modified"), a driver that swaps the index via CORPUS_INDEX_PATH (scripts/run-step4-post3b.sh:35), and recorded machine-readable results for three index states. On 2026-04-21 it measured a claim-pool scale-up from 1,145 to 4,921 claims -- 4.3x, precisely the concept-to-claim jump now proposed. Result (results/step4-post3b-2026-04-21/POST-3B-SUMMARY.md): average quality 0.794 -> 0.789 (delta -0.005); 4 of 6 prompts regressed; Bowin, Caston, Nussbaum, O'Gorman, Frede and White were CROWDED OUT of the prose on 3 prompts. Root cause recorded in that summary: TF scoreCandidate with no length normalization + fixed maxAuthors=8 + top-30 pool. This is the granularity ceiling, measured. Adding claim-level records to an unchanged retrieval contract makes drafting output slightly WORSE.

(2) CLAIM-LEVEL AND CLAUSE-LEVEL MATERIAL ALREADY EXISTS AND IS 100% UNREACHABLE. The sandbox holds 4,961 claims across 24 sources; 4,615 (93.0%) carry grounding.char_start / char_end -- genuine CHARACTER SPANS, the thing the audit says exists nowhere. Plus Toulmin decomposition (ground/warrant/qualifier/rebuttal), speaker, stance, use_mention, faithfulness verdict, and 14,811 concept-mentions each hung on an ontology_node with provenance {bekker, chunk_id, char_start, char_end} -- the exact wiring from claim level up to the existing concept graph. grep for production-sandbox|claims.jsonl|concept-mentions|bridge-candidates across src/ and scripts/ returns ZERO hits. Seven sources (Caston 1995, Frede 1992, Nussbaum 1985, O'Gorman 2005, Papachristou 2013, White 1985, Bowin 2017) have BOTH a concept-level corpus/index entry and a claim-level sandbox index -- a ready-made paired sample the A/B/C plan never used.

(3) A CONCEPT-LEVEL PARSE DEFECT PROPAGATED INTO AND DESTROYED 95% OF THE CLAIM-LEVEL BRIDGE WORK. 42 of 72 compiled cross-pipeline hooks (58%) have an empty targetConcept; cross-author-utils.ts:473-474 uses t.includes(targetLower), and in JS t.includes("") is always true, so every empty-target hook is a candidate for EVERY topic. Simulated over 6 realistic dissertation topics, 4 of 6 select an empty-target hook as the MANDATORY THEORETICAL SYNTHESIS -- rendering "X (Aristotle) <-> ? ()" plus the directive "Both authors MUST be cited with direct textual evidence" (gold-standard-prompt-builder.ts:708-717). Downstream: 525 of 552 sandbox bridge-candidates (95%) are anchored on an empty-target hook; 465 of those 525 were judged "unrelated". Of the 27 anchored on a well-formed hook, 25 (93%) were usable. A 6x yield difference decided entirely by whether the upstream markdown parsed.

The programme's diagnosis is correct: this is an addressing, schema and wiring problem, not an authoring problem. But the migration spec's disposition rule (:58) proposes DEFERRING Dissertation and Veri(dis)similitude -- the two entries holding the only working claim-level schemas in corpus/index -- on the grounds that they are "the user's own work". That rule is exactly inverted relative to the goal.
what_the_plan_actually_specifies:
FOUR DOCUMENTS, THREE DIFFERENT JOBS.

corpus-index-usage-plan.md (CONSUMPTION, 2026-03-09, status ACTIVE). Section 1 is a static hand-maintained inventory table (5 pipelines, 14 texts, 88 units, ~172 nodes, ~896 edges, ~612 lemmas, 25 graphs) plus a file-location tree. Section 2 gives five usage recipes: 2A single-author deep dive (concept-matrix.csv -> phase2-*.md -> bekker-index -> corpus-ontology tensions -> /god-write); 2B a six-phase cross-author trace (manual index reconnaissance -> construct prompt -> execute god-write with a 13-flag anti-hallucination stack -> internal 3-stage v1/investigate/v2 pipeline -> 7-item quality validation -> feedback loop); 2C tension-driven chapter structure; 2D terminology concordance; 2E a 11-step writing-session workflow with a copy-paste standard-flags block. Section 3 asserts a "bridge architecture" (shared 11 relations, 10 domains, pre-mapped cross-pipeline hooks) and a 9-row integration-surface table. Section 4 parks Phase 5 (cross-pipeline integration) pending the user's dissertation framework. Section 5 is a 4-checkbox maintenance protocol plus a 4-step "adding new texts" recipe and a 4-case correction recipe. Section 6 is an 11-row file-type quick reference. Section 7 is a 5-row decision log. No schema is defined anywhere; every artifact is identified by filename glob.

archon-corpus-index-migration-spec.md (MIGRATION, 2026-06-24, build-ready). Section 0 states two load-bearing truths: import from per-entry SOURCE files not compiled-index.json (which is lossy by construction), and adapter coverage is the long pole. Section 1 defines 14 new corpus_* CozoDB relations (entries, concepts, concept_terms, reasoning_edges, tensions, bridges, roda_crosswalks, debates, lemmas, claims, interlocutors/design_principles/ro_hooks, concept_chunks, vec_corpus_concepts + HNSW). Section 2 names 8 adapter families with crown-jewel fields, plus 2a a mandatory CSV dialect normalizer and 2b four field-mapping gotchas. Section 3 unifies 5 tension geometries into a superset. Section 4 specifies the Datalog retriever reproducing 3 prompt blocks at caps 12/3/5 plus a mandatory bridge, with a substring-not-token scorer correction and recursive graph traversal. Section 5 corrects fastembed API/cache/prefix details. Section 6 links concepts to doc_chunks by HNSW anchor-phrase resolution at cosine >= 0.9. Section 7 replaces the Python compiler with an analysis-entry SKILL driving an in-tree Rust importer. Section 8 sequences P0 through P7 with P0.5 census inserted as the long pole and P5 line-for-line parity vs live TS as the HARD cutover gate. Section 9 lists 6 open items and 5 self-contained risks.

index-system-ab-c-evaluation-plan.md (EVALUATION, 2026-05-01, "Designed, not yet executed"). A three-way controlled comparison on De Anima Gamma 3 (Bekker 427a17-429a9): Index A document-oriented (phase2 markdown + JSON manifests + mmd + appendices), Index B atom-oriented (claims.jsonl / concept-mentions.jsonl / bridge-candidates.jsonl in the production sandbox), Index C fused. A process firewall forbids reading phase2-da-04.md during Phase B. Each phase emits a PDF report plus think-aloud logging. Phase D is a post-mortem on five axes (time to first draft, citation density and traceability, narrative coherence, cross-author bridge richness, tension surfacing) with a concrete-recommendations section. Section 4 pre-registers six hypotheses H1-H6, of which H6 predicts the next-gen pipeline should feed B atoms into A's narrative pipeline. Section 5 lists five deliverables, Section 6 estimates ~5 hours, Section 7 leaves five open questions to resolve at execution time, Section 8 lists three prerequisites.

archon-corpus-index-comparison-report.md (DECISION, 2026-06-24). Concludes migrate-and-preserve, not replace: our analytical schema wins on 5 of 8 dimensions, Archon wins only on graph substrate. Section 3 prioritises 7 port items with effort ratings. Section 4 lists 6 things to adopt from Archon. Section 5 records three critical corrections from an adversarial pass, including the precise lossiness truth. Section 6 lists 5 genuinely-open items. Section 8 sequences schema+importer -> retriever -> SKILL, keeping the TS pipeline live until parity.

defects.defect: Section 4 mandates reproducing loadCorpusIndexContext at caps 12 ontology nodes / 3 hooks / 5 tensions with exact render templates, and :138 makes a line-for-line parity diff against the live TS the HARD cutover gate. Parity with a concept-level retriever is the wrong target for a claim/clause-level index: it freezes the prompt-side budget at ~20 index lines per draft call regardless of how many claim records exist behind it.
defects.consequence_observed: Verified in src/god-agent/universal/corpus-index-provider.ts:101-103 (maxNodes 12, maxHooks 3, maxTensions 5) and cross-author-utils.ts:498 (bridges hard-capped at 1). MEASURED consequence at tmp/analysis-upgrade/production-sandbox/results/step4-post3b-2026-04-21/POST-3B-SUMMARY.md: growing the claim pool 1,145 -> 4,921 (4.3x) moved average quality 0.794 -> 0.789 (delta -0.005), regressed 4 of 6 prompts, and crowded Bowin, Caston, Nussbaum, O'Gorman, Frede and White OUT of the prose on 3 prompts. The summary names the mechanism: TF scoreCandidate with no length normalization plus fixed maxAuthors=8 plus top-30 pool.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Do not specify parity as a gate. Specify the retrieval CONTRACT change first, before any authoring: (a) two-stage retrieval -- concept nodes select a candidate set, claim records are then retrieved WITHIN the selected concepts, so claim count never competes with concept count; (b) per-source quota so no author can be crowded out by a denser author; (c) length-normalised or per-source-normalised scoring; (d) an explicit claim budget (e.g. 24 claim lines) that is additive to, not carved out of, the 12/3/5 concept budget. Gate: source-coverage retention >= baseline on a frozen prompt suite. Land this BEFORE authoring a single claim record.

defects.defect: The defer/special adapter row explicitly proposes deciding import-vs-defer for Dissertation, Veri(dis)similitude (Salvo MA), Game-Behavior Method, Uncomfortable Situations and Heidegger&Rhetoric on the stated rationale 'these are the user's own work or method artifacts, not third-party analyses'. That rationale selects for provenance, not for schema value, and it deprioritises exactly the entries that hold the only proven claim-level schemas in the repository.
defects.consequence_observed: corpus/index/Dissertation/_run-history/2026-05-20T0058/_per-section/DISS-03-A3/phase2-claims.json carries 156 claims with claim_id, location.{line_start,line_end}, claim_type, logical_role, supports[], supported_by[], support_tier (8-tier), coined-term and interpretive flags, remediation, plus claim_count_target '140-180' vs claim_count_actual 156 and schema_version 'DISSERTATION-ANALYSIS-PIPELINE-PLAN-v1.4-8.1.1'. This is the only entry in corpus/index with a machine-checkable density gate and a plan version stamped into the artifact. Both Dissertation and Veri(dis)similitude are also absent from compile-corpus-index.py TEXT_DIRS (:34-129), so they contribute zero nodes today.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Invert the disposition rule. Rank entries for first-class treatment by SCHEMA MATURITY against the claim/clause target, not by authorship. Mandate that the new claim record schema be derived from the union of the three proven ones already on disk: Dissertation phase2-claims.json (support tiers, supports/supported_by graph, line anchors, density target-vs-actual), the sandbox claims.jsonl (Toulmin ground/warrant/qualifier/rebuttal, speaker, stance, use_mention, grounding.char_start/char_end, faithfulness), and Uexkull's Claim|Evidence type|Strength|Page ref. Name Dissertation and Veri(dis)similitude as the two REFERENCE implementations, not deferrals.

defects.defect: The plan asserts cross-pipeline hooks are pre-built, trustworthy bridges -- ':82 Each pipeline\'s cross-pipeline hooks file is a pre-built bridge. You don\'t need to re-read the primary texts to find connections'; ':293 Cross-pipeline hooks (pre-mapped connection points between pipelines)'; ':327 You don\'t need to discover connections'. It specifies no validity predicate for a hook and no gate that a hook must have a non-empty target. The worked example at :73 cites de-anima Hook 2 and Hook 4, both of which happen to be from the healthy minority, so the exemplar masks the failure mode.
defects.consequence_observed: Measured on corpus/index/compiled-index.json: 42 of 72 compiled hooks (58%) have an empty targetConcept, 4 have empty bridge text, and 41 carry a 13-character stub bridge ('[INTERP-high]'). hook-de-anima-07 has sourceConcept 'Summary Matrix', targetText '', targetConcept '', bridge '' -- a markdown parse artifact registered as a bridge and tagged INTERP-high. Well-formed hooks additionally leak markup into data: targetConcept 'BCAP on delta-upsilon-nu-alpha-mu-iota-sigma [INTERP-high]'.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Define a bridge as a typed record with a REQUIRED non-empty {source_id, source_entry, target_id, target_entry, bridge_text >= N chars, evidence_locus on BOTH sides}, and make a bridge with an empty endpoint a hard validation failure that blocks registration. Require every bridge endpoint to resolve to an existing node id in the registry (referential integrity check), not to a free-text concept name. Add a pre-registration check that rejects any parsed record whose name field still contains '[INTERP-' or other markup.

defects.defect: Section 4 mandates reproducing the MANDATORY THEORETICAL SYNTHESIS render verbatim -- '**Bridge [id]:** src (srcAuthor) <-> tgt (tgtAuthor)' plus 'Both authors MUST be cited with direct textual evidence' -- with no precondition that the bridge have two endpoints. The spec ports a directive that can command citation of a non-existent author.
defects.consequence_observed: src/god-agent/shared/cross-author-utils.ts:473-474 filters with `t.includes(sourceLower) || sourceLower.includes(t)` and the same for target; when targetLower is '' the JS expression t.includes('') is always true, so all 42 empty-target hooks become candidates for EVERY topic. computeMatchScore (:424) guards empties but the FILTER does not, and the tie-break at :489-491 promotes INTERP-high (58 of 72). Simulated over 6 realistic dissertation topics: boredom/attention/virtual/reality -> hook-de-anima-07 ('Summary Matrix', empty target, empty bridge, score 0); pedagogy/classroom/learning/outcomes -> same; social/presence/virtual/worlds -> hook-metaphysics-01 (empty target); rhetorical/incorporation/avatar -> hook-metaphysics-14 (empty target). 4 of 6 realistic Part III topics get a MANDATORY, MUST-cite directive pointing at nothing. gold-standard-prompt-builder.ts:712-713 renders the missing side as '?' and :710-711 calls it 'a verified, high-confidence interpretive link'.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Require the bridge selector to reject any candidate with an empty endpoint before scoring, and require the mandatory-bridge block to be OMITTED (not degraded to '?') when no candidate scores > 0. Specify that any prompt block asserting 'verified' must carry a verification field on the record it renders, and that the tag INTERP-high may not be emitted as 'verified'. Add an assertion test over the whole hook table: zero hooks with an empty endpoint may exist in the compiled artifact.

defects.defect: Section 2C tells the writer to 'Browse tensions -> tension-edges.json (Aristotle), tension-edges.json (B&T), etc.' and the file-type table :399 describes tension-edges.json only as 'Argument structure -- productive contradictions to build chapters around'. No field names, no required keys, no example record. Twelve entries then authored twelve different shapes.
defects.consequence_observed: 11 tension-edges.json files on disk carry 8 distinct shapes: node_a/node_b/dependency_edge/conflict_edge (Aristotle 12, BT 9, Rickert 7, BCAP 7, H&R 12, FCM 7 -- FCM additionally adds locus_a/locus_b); nodeA/nodeB/type (Uexkull 10); wendt_position/relation/against (Wendt 12); pole_A/pole_B (Uncomfortable 15); tension_id/label/description/supporting_units (In-Game 12); tension_id/label/pentad_terms_involved plus a separate unmatched_raw_tensions array (Grammar of Motives 16 + 21). compile-corpus-index.py:1125-1129 requires node_a|nodeA AND node_b|nodeB and returns None otherwise, so Wendt, Uncomfortable, In-Game and Grammar contribute ZERO. Verified: compiled-index.json holds 64 tensionEdges from exactly 7 texts; 55 authored tensions plus 21 unmatched raw are lost.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Ship a versioned JSON Schema file for every record type in the new plan, checked into the repo, and make schema validation a blocking pre-registration step. For tensions specifically: one shape with required {tension_id, entry_id, endpoint_a{node_id,label}, endpoint_b{node_id,label}, relation, directed, evidence_locus_a, evidence_locus_b, description}. Forbid per-entry field naming. Make the compiler FAIL LOUDLY (non-zero exit, named file, named record index) on any record it cannot normalise, instead of silently returning None.

defects.defect: The usage plan makes concept-matrix.csv and *-edges.csv the primary entry points (:58 'Open concept-matrix.csv, scan the row for aisthesis'; :402 the file-type table) without defining a single column. The migration spec :61 later specifies a header-sniffing dialect normalizer but scopes it to '>=10 header layouts (verified)'.
defects.consequence_observed: Measured across 240 CSVs (219 of them *edges*.csv): 47 DISTINCT header lines, not 10. The long tail includes a fully quoted dialect '\"source\",\"relation\",\"target\",\"locus\",\"note\"'; an 11-column edge_id,contributor,source_type,source_id,relation,target_type,target_id,target_label,evidence_locus,strength,note; source,target,relation,domain,weight,units,evidence (relation in col 3); source_claim,relation,edge_domain,target,note,location (target in col 4); src,rel,dst,book_page,note; and two byte-differing variants of the same nominal 5-column header. The normalizer as scoped would silently mis-column roughly the entire long tail.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Specify ONE canonical edge record with fixed required columns {edge_id, entry_id, source_id, relation, target_id, domain, evidence_locus, provenance, note} and forbid new dialects outright. Provide a one-time migration mapping table covering all 47 observed headers (enumerate them in the plan, do not say 'at least N'). Require the loader to reject any file whose header is not byte-identical to the canonical header after BOM/CRLF normalisation, and to name the offending file.

defects.defect: The 'Adding New Texts' recipe is four steps: create a plan from the pipeline template, execute Phases 0-4, add cross-pipeline hooks, update the Integration Surfaces table. None of the four is 'register the directory in scripts/compile-corpus-index.py TEXT_DIRS'. Registration is the single step that makes an entry reachable at runtime, and the plan never mentions it.
defects.consequence_observed: compile-corpus-index.py:34-129 hardcodes 19 directories in TEXT_DIRS. 27 entry directories exist. The 8 unregistered entries -- Dissertation, Veri(dis)similitude (Salvo MA), Game-Behavior Analysis Method (Burke x Calleja), Red Dead Redemption 2 (Salvo Playthrough), Red Dead Redemption 2 Secondary (2019-2023), Aristotelian Emotion Secondary (1975-2015), Aristotelian Motion and Time Secondary, Aristotelian Phantasia Secondary (1985-2017) -- contribute exactly zero nodes, zero tensions, zero anything to compiled-index.json. That is 30% of the corpus. Aristotelian Phantasia Secondary alone holds ~2,406 dict-shaped records across 8 articles plus 708 edge rows; RDR2 Secondary is one of only 2 entries in the whole index with a quality-gates-report.md.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Replace the hardcoded registry with directory auto-discovery plus a per-entry entry.json declaring {entry_id, adapter, schema_version, expected_record_counts}. Make 'entry is discoverable and produces >0 records at runtime' the FIRST gate of the creation plan, evaluated before any content authoring. Add a CI-style reachability report that lists, per entry, records-on-disk vs records-reaching-runtime, and fails if any entry is at zero.

defects.defect: Both documents correctly identify that *-edges.csv reasoning edges reach nothing, and the migration spec makes the dialect normalizer a MIGRATION-time component (P0.5) whose payoff arrives only at P7 cutover. Neither document instructs authors to stop producing unreachable edges in the meantime, and neither quantifies the loss.
defects.consequence_observed: grep -c 'edges.csv' scripts/compile-corpus-index.py returns 0 -- the compiler has never read a single edge CSV. 19,989 edge rows exist on disk across 219 files. compiled-index.json contains 701 ontologyNodes, 72 crossPipelineHooks, 64 tensionEdges and 1,722 canonicalTerms -- 837 records total. Reachability of the authored reasoning graph is 0 of 19,989.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Make reachability a per-entry ACCEPTANCE criterion, not a migration outcome: an entry is not complete until a named script reads its records and a named runtime consumer renders them. Require the creation plan to state, for each artifact type it asks authors to produce, the exact consumer (file:function) that reads it. Any artifact type with no named consumer must not be authored.

defects.defect: The entire Section 8 phase structure is corpus-scale: P0.5 'corpus census + adapter coverage', P2 'tension unification (4-shape superset)', P3 'remaining adapters', P5 'line-for-line diff vs live TS'. At N=1 -- creating an entry for a single new article -- there is no census, no adapter family, no cross-entry superset and no parity corpus. Every gate in the plan evaluates to zero or is inapplicable.
defects.consequence_observed: No per-entry acceptance criteria exist anywhere in the four plans. Consequence in the built corpus: only 2 of 27 entries have a quality-gates-report.md (Wendt, RDR2 Secondary) and only 1 has machine-readable metrics; several manifests declare phases pending that are complete on disk, and BCAP section 3B contradicts its own companion CSV in every line.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Write the gates at N=1 FIRST and make corpus-level checks a rollup of them. Per-entry, per-source gates that are non-vacuous at N=1: schema validation passes; every claim record resolves to a char span in a stored fulltext; claim density within a declared target band (record target AND actual, as Dissertation phase2-claims.json already does); zero dangling node/edge references; zero duplicate ids within the entry; every locus verified against the source PDF by a page-offset probe; entry appears in the reachability report with >0 records. Emit a machine-readable gates.json per entry, mandatory, not optional.

defects.defect: Status 'Designed, not yet executed' -- and it never was. The single experiment in the entire programme designed to answer whether a claim-level index beats a concept-level one was written on 2026-05-01 and left unrun while the concept-level authoring programme continued to 27 entries and 1,759 files. Nothing in the plan makes execution a precondition for continued authoring.
defects.consequence_observed: tmp/index-ab-c-evaluation/ does not exist. None of the five deliverables at :208-213 (Report-A/B/C/D PDFs, AB-C-comparison-log.md) exist anywhere on disk. Meanwhile Index B grew from the plan's cited 79 claims / 319 mentions / 23 bridges for aristotle-da-3-3 (still exactly correct today) to 4,961 claims / 14,811 mentions / 552 bridges across 24 sources -- and remains referenced by zero files in src/ or scripts/.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Make the measurement the FIRST deliverable, not the last. Sequence: (1) land index-path injection and the metrics emitter; (2) run the paired baseline on the 7 dual-represented sources; (3) only then authorise bulk claim-level authoring, and only for the record types the measurement showed move a metric. Add a standing rule: no more than N entries may be authored past an unmeasured design change.

defects.defect: Index B is defined to live at tmp/analysis-upgrade/production-sandbox/data/corpus/index/, the plan acknowledges at :246 that sandbox paths 'may or may not be stable across system updates', and it contains no instruction to promote Index B out of tmp/ or to wire it to anything. Evaluation is specified; adoption is not.
defects.consequence_observed: 4,961 claims with 4,615 character spans, 14,811 ontology-linked concept mentions and 552 bridge candidates sit in tmp/. grep across src/ and scripts/ for production-sandbox|claims.jsonl|concept-mentions|bridge-candidates returns 0 hits. The richest clause-adjacent asset in the repository is invisible to the drafting runtime and to the audit that concluded clause level is 'genuinely absent everywhere'.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Require every experiment to declare its promotion path and its owner before it runs: where the artifact lands if it wins, which consumer reads it, and what deletes it if it loses. Forbid new index artifacts under tmp/. As an immediate action, promote the sandbox JSONL streams into corpus/index/_atoms/<source-slug>/ under the new schema, since they are already at target granularity for 24 sources.

defects.defect: H4 predicts 'B cross-author bridges > A cross-author bridges by an order of magnitude' and axis 4 at :167 asks 'How many cross-author conceptual links surfaced in each?'. The metric is a COUNT of bridges, with quality relegated to a parenthetical ('genuine vs. cosmetic?') that has no rubric. A layer with 15% precision would confirm the hypothesis.
defects.consequence_observed: Measured on the actual artifact: 552 bridge candidates, of which 467 (85%) carry relation 'unrelated', 100% carry needsReview true, and 473 carry confidence 'high' (confidence is in the JUDGEMENT, not the bridge). 525 of 552 (95%) are anchored on a hook with an empty targetConcept -- top three anchors are hook-de-anima-07 (184), hook-metaphysics-01 (178), hook-metaphysics-02 (163), all empty-target. Of the 525 broken-anchor candidates only 60 (11%) are non-unrelated; of the 27 well-anchored candidates 25 (93%) are. Only 8 distinct hooks of 72 were ever used as anchors, because getActiveBridges caps at 1 and the empty-string bug makes the same few always win.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Never count records as a quality metric. Specify PRECISION metrics with denominators: usable-bridge rate (non-unrelated / total), anchor-validity rate (candidates whose anchor has two non-empty endpoints), and anchor coverage (distinct anchors exercised / anchors available). Set a pre-registered threshold (e.g. usable-bridge rate >= 0.5) and require the anchor-validity gate to pass BEFORE any derivative generation runs against those anchors.

defects.defect: The Phase D five-axis comparison is the plan's only evaluation instrument, and 3 of 5 axes are unmeasurable as written. Axis 3 'Does each report read as a coherent argument? Can a reader follow the dialectical structure without prior knowledge? Where does each show stress?'. Axis 4 'Quality of those links (genuine vs. cosmetic)?'. Axis 5 'How well does each surface genuine philosophical tensions'. No scale, no rubric, no rater, no threshold, no inter-rater check.
defects.consequence_observed: No post-mortem was ever produced, so no axis was ever scored. The two axes that ARE measurable (time to first draft; % of claims traceable to a page / exact span / faithfulness verdict) are precisely the two the sandbox harness later computed automatically -- indicating the plan's manual instrument was unnecessary for them and useless for the rest.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Every gate in the new plan must name (a) the computing script, (b) the numeric output, (c) the pass threshold, (d) the artifact the number is written to. Ban prose gates. Where human judgement is genuinely required, specify a fixed rubric with anchored levels and require two raters on a random 10% with a reported agreement statistic.

defects.defect: Every adapter maps pdf_pages, book_page and locus straight through to the target relations, and :67 trusts book-level-ontology.json centrality as 'trusted'. No step anywhere in the spec verifies that a declared page offset is correct, or that it is constant.
defects.consequence_observed: Aristotle: 33 of 34 unit records carry pdf_pages from a superseded linear offset with errors up to 47 pages; the bekker-index has 101 of 188 loci off by more than 2 pages. Rickert declares pdf_page_offset 20 which is both wrong AND non-constant, drifting 18 -> 15. Under the spec as written all of that migrates verbatim into corpus_claims.locus and corpus_lemmas.locus, laundering bad addresses into a new database.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Mandate a page-offset PROBE as a blocking gate per source: sample K >= 5 loci spread across the document, extract the text at the declared offset, assert a token match against the recorded quote/heading, and record probe results in the entry's gates.json. Treat a non-constant offset as a hard failure requiring a per-range offset table, not a scalar. Forbid importing any locus from a source whose probe has not passed.

defects.defect: corpus_claims is defined as {claim_id => entry_id, local_id, text, locus, unit} -- five fields, with locus an opaque string. It carries no span, no tier, no supports/supported_by, no quote, no faithfulness verdict, no stance, no speaker. This is the target schema for the crown-jewel record type, and it is strictly poorer than three schemas already sitting on disk.
defects.consequence_observed: On disk today: Dissertation phase2-claims.json has 19 fields including location.{line_start,line_end}, supports[], supported_by[], support_tier across 8 tiers, interpretive flags and remediation. tmp/analysis-upgrade/.../claims.jsonl has quote, claim, ground, warrant, qualifier, rebuttal, claim_type, stance, use_mention, speaker, key_concepts, chunk_id, pdf_pages, grounding{quote_match, match_ratio, char_start, char_end, matched_span, extracted_anchor}, faithfulness, faithfulness_note. Uexkull has Claim|Evidence type|Strength|Page ref. Migrating any of these into the 5-field shape DESTROYS the addressing the goal requires.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Specify the claim record as the union of what is proven: {claim_id, entry_id, source_id, unit_id, claim_text, quote_verbatim, span{doc_id, char_start, char_end, sha256_of_fulltext}, locus{page, book_page, bekker|timestamp|line_range}, claim_type (closed enum), stance (closed enum), use_mention (closed enum), speaker, support_tier (closed enum), supports[], supported_by[], concept_ids[], faithfulness (closed enum), faithfulness_note, provenance}. Mark span REQUIRED for any claim whose quote is present. Publish the enums in the plan, not in the executing agent's head.

defects.defect: 'Edges live only in .mmd (open item)' is recorded for exactly two adapter families -- aristotle-manifest (:55) and heidegger-sz (:56). The inventory implies .mmd-only edges are a two-family problem.
defects.consequence_observed: Measured: 67 .mmd files across 15 entries -- Aristotle 8, Uexkull 5, VR Pedagogy Secondary 5, Uncomfortable 5, RDR2 Secondary 5, In-Game 5, Heidegger and Rhetoric 5, Being and Time 5, Boredom Secondary 5, Phantasia Secondary 5, Grammar of Motives 5, BCAP 4, Rickert 3, Boredom Experiment 1, Rhetoric of Motives 1. That spans at least five of the eight named adapter families, including the two 'crown jewel' families burke-monograph and calleja-monograph. The inventory is incomplete and understates the open item by roughly 7x in entries.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Require a machine-generated artifact census (extension x entry x count x named consumer) as an input to the plan, regenerated at plan time, not a hand-typed table. Explicitly decide the .mmd disposition ONCE for the whole corpus: either .mmd is derived output only (and every edge it draws must exist in the canonical edge store first -- add a check that every .mmd edge round-trips), or .mmd is a source and needs a parser. Do not leave it per-family.

defects.defect: The tension superset in Section 3 enumerates five geometries: csv-edge, wendt-position, uexkull-nodes, compiled-dual, cluster-debate. It is presented as complete for the inspected shapes and drives the P2 deliverable.
defects.consequence_observed: Eight distinct shapes exist on disk. The superset omits pole_A/pole_B (corpus/index/Uncomfortable Situations/_synthesis/tension-edges.json, 15 tensions), tension_id/label/description/supporting_units/page_anchors (corpus/index/In-Game (Calleja 2011)/_synthesis/tension-edges.json, 12), tension_id/label/pentad_terms_involved plus a parallel unmatched_raw_tensions array (corpus/index/A Grammar of Motives (Burke 1945)/_synthesis/tension-edges.json, 16 + 21 raw), and the FCM variant that adds locus_a/locus_b. So the spec covers 1 of the 4 shapes that currently yield zero runtime edges.

defects.defect: 'corpus_claims.local_id is required but claims[].id exists in only 2 of 7 Wendt units -> synthesize stable local_ids (e.g. {unit}-c{n}) or :put fails.' A positional counter is not stable: inserting or deleting a claim renumbers every subsequent one, silently breaking every reference into that unit.
defects.consequence_observed: Wendt: 139 claim objects, 91 lack ids, 20 collide. Boredom Secondary: ids collide across 6 units. Corpus-wide the audit filed 10 id-collision and 44 dangling-reference defects. Synthesised positional ids are the mechanism that turns an edit into a dangling reference.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Require ids to be assigned once, at authoring time, and never derived from position. Specify a deterministic content-addressed id (entry_id + unit_id + sha256(claim_text)[0:8]) so the same claim always gets the same id and a moved claim keeps it. Make id uniqueness within the corpus and referential integrity of every supports/supported_by/concept_id a blocking validation.

defects.defect: 'triple-pagination -> one opaque composite locus (don\'t parse)'. The spec explicitly forbids parsing the finest locator that Being and Time carries (Heidegger H-page / English page / PDF page), collapsing three resolvable addresses into one unqueryable string.
defects.consequence_observed: Being and Time is the entry with 108 claim records as markdown table rows and 299 edges in fenced JSON -- content that is ~90% of the way to the target and 0% of the way in form. Storing its addresses as an opaque composite makes the claim rows permanently unaddressable at the level the goal requires.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Specify locus as a STRUCTURED object with named, individually-queryable subfields and an edition tag: {edition, book_page, translation_page, pdf_page, native_locator{kind: bekker|H|section|timestamp|line_range, value}}. Forbid opaque composite loci anywhere. Require at least one subfield to be machine-verifiable against the source.

defects.defect: ':110 v1 = one vector per concept (fastest path to BLOCK-1 parity); per-phrase embeddings are a follow-on.' ':118 most concepts are locus-only (no chunk row) ... Provenance coverage is uneven by design; downstream checks must tolerate locus-only concepts.' The embedding layer is specified at concept granularity, and provenance is made optional by explicit design.
defects.consequence_observed: One vector per concept means the retrievable unit remains the concept even after migration -- the ceiling is reproduced in the vector layer, not just the scorer. And 'downstream checks must tolerate locus-only concepts' removes the only pressure that would have forced spans to exist. Result on disk: nothing in 1,759 corpus/index files carries a sentence offset, character span or bbox; the finest locator is a page, page range, Bekker line pair or video timestamp.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Embed at CLAIM granularity (one vector per claim record) from v1, with the concept vector as a derived centroid. Make span presence a REQUIRED field for any claim carrying a quote, and report span coverage per entry as a gate metric with a floor (the sandbox already achieves 93.0%, so set the floor at 90% and treat regressions as failures). Replace 'tolerate locus-only' with 'locus-only claims are quarantined and reported, not silently accepted'.

defects.defect: 'The TS pipeline stays live and authoritative until the Datalog retriever reaches line-for-line parity (P5); cutover is the last phase.' Combined with P5 rated XL and P7 cutover last, nothing the migration imports reaches the drafting runtime until the final phase of a multi-phase XL project. There is no incremental-value milestone and no fallback if P5 stalls.
defects.consequence_observed: The migration was specified 2026-06-24 and has not cut over. Meanwhile the runtime input remains a single file: src/god-agent/shared/jsonl-loaders.ts:198-200 resolves <cwd>/corpus/index/compiled-index.json and nothing else, and corpus-index-provider.ts:73-77 explicitly ignores its own indexPath argument ('parameter preserved for API compatibility but ignored'). Everything authored since June reaches drafting only through that one 837-record file.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Sequence for earliest reachable value: land the schema plus a loader that reads the new records ALONGSIDE the existing compiled index in the current runtime, before any storage migration. Require every phase to end with a state where at least one new record type is visible in a rendered prompt block. Make 'records reaching runtime' a per-phase reported number that must strictly increase.

defects.defect: The Section 1 inventory is hand-typed and approximate -- '~172 nodes', '~896 edges', '~612 lemmas', '~180', '~156', '~120', '~25', '~30', '~37'. Section 5's maintenance protocol is four unowned checkboxes ('After adding a new text/pipeline to the index') with no gate, no script and no owner.
defects.consequence_observed: Reality on 2026-07-29: 27 entries (not 5 pipelines), 1,759 files, 701 compiled ontologyNodes, 19,989 edge rows on disk, 64 tension edges reaching runtime. Approximate counts are unfalsifiable, so drift is undetectable -- directly seeding the largest defect class in the audit (count-mismatch, 66 of 551) and the manifests that declare phases pending which are complete on disk.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Forbid hand-typed counts in the plan and in any manifest. Require every count to be emitted by a named script into a machine-readable metrics file, with the script path recorded next to the number. Add a reconciliation gate: manifest-declared counts must equal script-computed counts or registration fails.

defects.defect: Phase V 'Quality Validation' is the plan's only output gate: 7 items, of which 3 are unmeasurable as written. ':208 Style match: Long sentences (~31 words avg), author-prominent citations, formal register' has no threshold and no tool; ':206 Source coverage: All three authors should appear with citations' has no computing step; ':207 Quotation fidelity: >=70% similarity' names a number but no command. All 7 are manual post-hoc human checks with no artifact.
defects.consequence_observed: No entry produced a quality report from this gate. Only 2 of 27 entries have a quality-gates-report.md at all, and only 1 carries machine-readable metrics. By contrast the same pipeline already emits, per run, citationEnforcement{totalCitations, validCitations, hallucinatedCitations, passRate, missingPageNumbers, correctionsMade}, qualityScore, retrievalStats and provenanceLedger -- none of which the plan asks anyone to record.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Replace the 7-item manual list with an emitted metrics record. Mandate that every drafting run writes a metrics JSON and that the entry-creation plan's acceptance gates read that JSON. Include the two metrics that already exist and already show failure: citationEnforcement.missingPageNumbers (17 of 20, i.e. 85% of citations unlocatable, in the recorded phantasia-action run) and provenanceLedger.claims.length (0, even in the 4,921-claim run).

defects.defect: Section 4 parks Phase 5 -- the step that would promote [INTERP-high] hooks to confirmed edges -- behind an input that never arrives ('Your dissertation framework description'). The plan therefore permanently defers the only specified verification of the bridge layer, while Sections 2 and 3 instruct writers to rely on that layer as if verified.
defects.consequence_observed: All 72 compiled hooks remain tagged INTERP-high (58), INTERP-med (8) or INTERP-low (6). None is confirmed. gold-standard-prompt-builder.ts:710-711 nonetheless renders whichever one wins as 'a verified, high-confidence interpretive link between primary sources in the corpus'. Decision-log entry U2 (:415) records the parking as deliberate.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Never gate a verification step on an unscheduled external input. Give every interpretive record a confidence field with an explicit lifecycle (proposed -> evidence-attached -> confirmed), require evidence on BOTH endpoints before promotion, and forbid the prompt layer from describing anything as 'verified' unless the record is in the confirmed state.

defects.defect: ':82 Each pipeline\'s cross-pipeline hooks file is a pre-built bridge' and the Section 3B integration-surface table present hooks as a symmetric, all-pipeline facility (columns for BCAP, B&T, Uexkull, Rickert). The compiler implements nothing of the kind.
defects.consequence_observed: compile-corpus-index.py:1244 globs only 'corpus/index/Aristotle - Complete Works/*-cross-pipeline-hooks.md'. All 72 compiled hooks have an Aristotle sourceText (Metaphysics 15, Physics 14, Rhetoric 9, De Anima 7, Movement of Animals 6, On Memory 6, Sense and Sensibilia 6, On Things Heard 5, On Colours 4). Every non-Aristotle entry's hooks reach runtime as zero, so the 9-row integration table at :303-313 describes connections that exist only in the plan.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: State the consumer's actual coverage in the plan, verified at plan time by running the consumer, not inferred from the authoring convention. Require bridges to be entry-agnostic: one bridge store, entry_id on each record, discovered by directory walk, with a per-entry bridge count in the reachability report.

defects.defect: The measurement instrument is a think-aloud protocol plus 'Total elapsed time', recorded by the same agent that is also the experimental subject, on a single passage, with a single rater and no repeats. H1's only quantitative prediction is a TIME ratio ('A approximately 0.4x B in elapsed time') -- the metric least connected to index quality.
defects.consequence_observed: Any delta produced by this design is unattributable: agent elapsed time varies with model load, context length and tool latency, none of which is index quality. Nothing in the plan repeats a condition, so no variance estimate is possible and no delta can be distinguished from noise.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Drop elapsed time as a primary metric. Use n >= 12 prompts x >= 2 arms x >= 3 seeds with a fixed seed list, and report per-metric mean and spread. Make the metrics index-sensitive and automatically computed (locator resolution rate, claim-ledger fill, quote-verifiability, source-coverage retention), so the writing agent is not also the instrument.

defects.defect: H3 asserts 'Every claim in B has character-level grounding and a faithfulness verdict' and predicts 'B traceability approximately 100% at character level'. The predicate was never checked against the artifact, and it is false.
defects.consequence_observed: Measured over all 4,961 sandbox claims: 4,615 (93.0%) carry char_start/char_end, not 100%; 226 have quote_match false; 120 carry no grounding object at all; faithfulness distribution is supported 3,417 / partial 1,258 / unchecked 245 / unsupported 40 / author-endorsed 1 -- so 245 claims have NO verdict; match_ratio median is 1.000 but the minimum is 0.083, i.e. a long tail of near-worthless matches counted as grounded. claim_type carries 15 uncontrolled values (subsidiary_claim, textual_claim, primary_thesis, critical_claim, interpretive_claim, exegetical_claim, methodological_claim, concession, thetic, predecessor_report, methodological_remark, definitional, empirical_observation, dialectical_refutation, dialectical_objection), with aristotle-da-3-3 using 'thetic' where every other source uses a different dialect.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: State hypotheses about artifacts as CHECKS to run, not predictions to assume, and run them before the experiment. Require closed enums for claim_type, stance, use_mention, support_tier and faithfulness, published in the plan and enforced at validation. Add a match_ratio floor (e.g. reject or quarantine below 0.85) so 'grounded' means something.

defects.defect: Phase B's inputs are three JSONL streams for the focal work plus 'claims.jsonl and concept-mentions.jsonl for each of the bridge-target authors named in section 2' -- ten more authors. The plan never specifies how anyone queries them: no index, no query tool, no CLI, no retrieval step.
defects.consequence_observed: Those streams now total 4,961 claims and 14,811 mentions. Reading them by hand is not a protocol. The absence of a query surface is also why the atom index was never adopted: there is no way to ask it anything. Confirmed by the zero grep hits for claims.jsonl / concept-mentions.jsonl across src/ and scripts/.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Require the new plan to ship a QUERY SURFACE alongside the schema, as a named deliverable with acceptance tests: given a topic, return the top-k claim records with their spans, their concept ids and their source. An index nobody can query cannot improve drafting regardless of how good its records are.

defects.defect: Section 7 leaves five design decisions open 'to Resolve at Execution Time', including scope (:235 full Gamma 3 or just the polemical middle) and corpus (:236 all bridge-target authors or a curated subset). A protocol whose scope and corpus are undecided cannot be pre-registered, so the six hypotheses at :174-201 are not falsifiable against any fixed procedure.
defects.consequence_observed: Section 8 lists resolving these as a prerequisite (:248), which combined with the unresolved questions gave the experiment a soft blocker that was never cleared -- one reason it sat undone for 15 months.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Resolve every scope decision inside the plan and pin the resulting configuration (prompt list, source list, seed list, arm definitions) into a version-controlled, SHA-recorded config file, exactly as the sandbox already does for canonical-suite.json. A plan with open scope questions is not executable.

defects.defect: The A/B/C design compares whole INDEX SYSTEMS on one passage rather than comparing the two representations of the SAME sources. It therefore confounds granularity with source coverage, with authoring style and with which authors happen to be present in each index.
defects.consequence_observed: A cheap, fully-controlled paired sample already exists and the plan does not use it: seven sources have BOTH a concept-level corpus/index entry and a claim-level sandbox index -- Caston 1995, Frede 1992, Nussbaum 1985, O'Gorman 2005, Papachristou 2013 and White 1985 in corpus/index/Aristotelian Phantasia Secondary (1985-2017), plus Bowin 2017 in corpus/index/Aristotelian Motion and Time Secondary. For Caston 1995 the concept-level entry offers 5 readings and 32 concepts; the claim-level index offers 55 span-anchored claims. For Papachristou 2013, 244 dict records with ~8 readings versus 312 span-anchored claims.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Specify a PAIRED design on identical sources: same 7 works, same prompts, only the record granularity differs. That isolates the variable the plan actually cares about and requires zero new authoring to run.

defects.defect: The Section 2 capability matrix rates our analytical schema 'OURS' on the strength of a 'claim ledger C1-C20' -- roughly 20 claims per unit -- and rates concept-to-source provenance as 'Parity' because ours carries page-level string loci while Archon carries chunk ids. The report's own scoring treats the concept-level ceiling as a win and never flags that neither side reaches clause level.
defects.consequence_observed: This framing is what allowed the migration spec to define corpus_claims with five fields and an opaque locus (:36) without anyone objecting. 20 claims per unit against roughly 320 units is the ~7-records-per-source regime the new goal replaces.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Score capability against the TARGET granularity, not against the alternative system. Add an explicit addressability dimension to any comparison matrix with levels: entry / unit / page / paragraph / sentence / character span, and report where each system actually lands.

defects.defect: Proposes corpus_concepts with `name PK` -- concept name as primary key. Names collide across texts, carry markup and Greek/German orthography variants, and change when prose is edited.
defects.consequence_observed: Measured in compiled-index.json: targetConcept values include 'BCAP on delta-upsilon-nu-alpha-mu-iota-sigma [INTERP-high]' -- the tag parsed into the key. canonicalTerms (1,722 entries) contains whole sentences such as 'Debate axis 9: social presence reliably predicts satisfaction/learning <-> effects inconsistent/assumed-not-demonstrated' plus bare English words 'technological', 'Presence' and 'control', all now in a corpus-wide greedy-match list. Uexkull has four mutually incompatible German orthographies coexisting, and the corrupted one is the one reaching runtime.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Opaque, stable, content-addressed ids for every record type; names are attributes with an orthography/variant list, never keys. Add a canonical-term admission gate: a term enters the global match list only if it is >= N characters, is not a stopword or bare common English word, and is declared in a per-entry terms file -- never harvested from a heading or a table cell by regex.

defects.defect: Three load-bearing definitions are left as Open items: the relation-verb census that decides which verbs project into corpus_tensions (:83), the two tokenizers and two thresholds the retriever must preserve per-consumer (:100), and six further items at :148 including the .mmd-to-CSV pre-pass and the tension-verb whitelist. With these open, P2 and P5 have no definition of done.
defects.consequence_observed: Both P2 and P5 are gated on behaviour that the spec cannot state, so 'complete' is unverifiable. Corpus-wide the relation vocabulary is uncontrolled -- the comparison report itself notes a ~36-value type vocabulary needing a fold to a controlled enum (:37).
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Resolve all vocabulary questions inside the plan by enumerating the closed sets. Publish the full relation enum, the domain enum and the tension-verb subset as literal lists. Any plan that ships with an open vocabulary ships with an unverifiable gate.

defects.defect: The file-type table classifies *.mmd as 'Visual concept maps for presentations or orientation' -- explicitly a rendering, not a data source. The migration spec later records that for two whole adapter families the edges exist ONLY in .mmd.
defects.consequence_observed: Two plans in the same programme disagree on whether 67 files across 15 entries are source or output. Under the usage plan's reading they are disposable; under the migration spec's they are the only copy of some edges. No plan resolves it, so authors were free to treat .mmd as either.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Declare a single directionality rule and enforce it: canonical store is authoritative, .mmd is generated from it, and a round-trip check asserts every edge drawn in any .mmd exists in the canonical store. Where .mmd is currently the only copy, schedule a one-time extraction as a named prerequisite with a record count.

defects.defect: Section 6 lists five 'still genuinely open' items with no owner, no resolution gate and no due phase. They propagate unchanged into the migration spec's Section 9 open items (:148).
defects.consequence_observed: Open item 1 (can doc_chunks carry arbitrary page/locus metadata) is the question on which clause-level addressing depends, and it is annotated '(Now answerable directly -- Archon source is local.)' -- i.e. it was cheap to answer and was still not answered. It remains unresolved in the June spec.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Forbid unowned open items. Every open question gets an owner, a resolution method, a deadline phase and a default decision that takes effect if unresolved -- so the plan cannot stall on an unanswered question.

defects.defect: 'Entries lacking book-level-ontology (Aristotle/Heidegger) get empty centrality_tier (acceptable -- it\'s not scored/rendered anyway).' Declaring a field unimportant is why it was never validated, and the claim about rendering is not safe.
defects.consequence_observed: compiled-index.json carries centralityTier on all 701 nodes with 12 distinct value shapes, including 4 overflow blobs up to 10,009 characters and markdown fragments such as 'peripheral --- ## 3b: global e', 'core ### important nodes (15)' and 'important ### peripheral nodes'. The field is corrupt in the compiled artifact regardless of whether the current renderer reads it, and any future consumer inherits the corruption.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Validate every field the schema declares, including ones no current consumer reads -- a value that violates its enum is a failure, not an acceptable blank. Add a max-length and enum check for every scalar field.

defects.defect: The spec's importer step is 'verify row counts (re-run idempotent)' with no stated source of expected counts, and the usage plan's only description of manifest.json is 'Unit metadata, PDF locations, tier assignments'. Neither makes the manifest an authoritative count declaration that anything checks.
defects.consequence_observed: Manifests across the corpus declare phases pending that are complete on disk and declare statistics contradicting their own companion CSVs (BCAP section 3B wrong in every line). Count-mismatch is the single largest defect category in the audit at 66 of 551.
defects.fix_for_new_plan: Make the manifest a CONTRACT: it declares expected counts per record type before authoring, the validator computes actuals after, and a mismatch blocks registration. Dissertation phase2-claims.json already demonstrates the pattern with claim_count_target '140-180' vs claim_count_actual 156 -- generalise it.

unspecified_gaps: No plan defines a SCHEMA for any artifact. All four describe artifacts by filename glob (usage plan :392-406 is an 11-row filename table; migration spec :49-58 is a family-to-layout table). Executing agents invented field names per entry, producing 8 tension shapes, 47 edge-CSV header dialects, 9 incompatible sub-schemas inside Boredom Secondary alone, and 24 header dialects in RDR2 Playthrough.

No plan states how an entry becomes REACHABLE at runtime. Registration in compile-corpus-index.py TEXT_DIRS (:34-129) is never mentioned by any plan, so 8 of 27 entries were authored without it and contribute zero records.

No plan states what the CONSUMER reads. Nothing tells authors that the compiler reads book-level-ontology.md and never book-level-ontology.json (compile-corpus-index.py:1199, :1221), so In-Game and Uncomfortable each authored 18 canonical positions into a JSON the pipeline never opens.

No plan defines controlled vocabularies. claim_type has 15 uncontrolled values in the sandbox; Boredom Secondary's stance field has 162 uncontrolled values with 195 nulls; the comparison report notes a ~36-value type vocabulary (:37) with no published enum.

No plan defines ID assignment. The migration spec only says to synthesize ids where missing (:64). Result: Wendt 91/139 claims without ids and 20 collisions, ids colliding across 6 Boredom units, 10 id-prefix-violation and 10 id-collision defects.

No plan requires locator verification. No page-offset probe, no quote round-trip, no assertion that a locus resolves. Result: Aristotle 33/34 records with offsets wrong by up to 47 pages; bekker-index 101/188 loci off by >2 pages; Rickert's declared offset both wrong and drifting.

No plan states a stored-fulltext requirement or a retention rule for it. In-Game's 995 line-range anchors were rendered worthless when /tmp/calleja-fulltext.txt was deleted (verified absent). Nothing anywhere records the fulltext hash the anchors point into.

No plan reconciles the content-filter policy with the goal. Two entries deliberately suppress verbatim text (In-Game ig-10-deep.json:434-441; Uncomfortable us-03-radcliffe.json:110,:234). A clause-level index needs the clause. No plan takes a position.

No plan defines a QUERY SURFACE. The A/B/C plan asks an agent to consult 14,811 JSONL rows (:126) with no tool. The usage plan's query method is human grep over markdown. No plan specifies how a claim record is retrieved by topic.
No plan defines what a quality report contains or requires one per entry. Result: 2 of 27 entries have a quality-gates-report.md, 1 has machine-readable metrics.

No plan specifies index-path injection, so no A/B is possible in the live tree. jsonl-loaders.ts:198-200 hard-resolves <cwd>/corpus/index/compiled-index.json and corpus-index-provider.ts:73-77 explicitly ignores its indexPath argument. The sandbox worked only because a forked src-worktree patched it (tmp/analysis-upgrade/production-sandbox/src-worktree/src/god-agent/shared/jsonl-loaders.ts:199,204 honours CORPUS_INDEX_PATH). That patch was never merged.

No plan requires the runtime to EMIT what the index contributed. corpusIndexContributions and injectedBridges have code paths (write-pipeline-orchestrator.ts:833-860, cli.ts:1616) but appear in 0 of the recorded step4 stdout.json files, so no run on record can show whether the index changed the prompt at all.

No plan sets a claim DENSITY target per source. Dissertation phase2-claims.json is the only artifact in the corpus carrying claim_count_target and claim_count_actual, and no plan asks for it. Result: 5 readings per article in Phantasia Secondary against 155-312 claims per article for the same works in the sandbox.

No plan states what happens to an entry authored under a superseded schema version. Only Dissertation stamps schema_version into its artifacts. Nothing else can be migrated safely because nothing declares what shape it is.

No plan defines duplicate-run handling. corpus/index/Dissertation carries two full run-histories (2026-05-13T1439 and 2026-05-20T0058) with identical claim files, so every claim exists twice on disk with no rule for which counts.
No plan specifies a budget or a cost model for claim-level authoring, though the sandbox recorded one ($20 for 3,776 claims from 15 papers; $1.80 for 6 prose-validation runs; ~$26.60 session total).
design_inputs: MEASUREMENT BEFORE AUTHORING. Land the harness first, as deliverable #1, and make it a precondition for bulk authoring. It is mostly built: freeze a prompt suite the way tmp/analysis-upgrade/production-sandbox/data/prompts/canonical-suite.json is frozen (SHA recorded in a manifest, marked immutable), and reuse scripts/run-step4-post3b.sh as the driver shape.

MAKE THE INDEX PATH INJECTABLE IN THE LIVE TREE. Port the sandbox patch: honour CORPUS_INDEX_PATH in src/god-agent/shared/jsonl-loaders.ts:198-200 (the sandbox fork already does this at src-worktree/.../jsonl-loaders.ts:199,204) and stop ignoring options.indexPath in src/god-agent/universal/corpus-index-provider.ts:73-77. ~20 LOC. Without it no A/B arm can be run without forking src again, and every future evaluation is blocked.

EMIT WHAT THE INDEX CONTRIBUTED. Wire corpusIndexContributions {ontologyNodesUsed, hooksInjected, tensionEdgesUsed} and injectedBridges[] (code paths exist at write-pipeline-orchestrator.ts:833-860 and cli.ts:1616) into the recorded run JSON. They are absent from all 6 step4 stdout.json files, so no existing run can show whether the index touched the prompt.

USE FOUR INDEX-SENSITIVE METRICS, NOT qualityScore. (a) Locator resolution rate -- fraction of emitted citations whose locator resolves to a span in a stored source; today's baseline is 3 of 20, since citationEnforcement.missingPageNumbers = 17 on the recorded phantasia-action run. (b) Claim-ledger fill -- provenanceLedger.claims.length; today's baseline is 0 even in the 4,921-claim run, so any claim-level index that leaves it at 0 has changed nothing. (c) Quote-verifiability -- fraction of quoted spans byte-matching a stored verbatim, via the existing QuotationFidelityValidator against grounding.matched_span. (d) Source-coverage retention -- set of cited authors diffed against baseline; this is the metric that caught the crowding-out regression and no concept-level plan had it. qualityScore moved only 0.005 across a 4.3x index change and must not be primary.

RUN THE PAIRED ARM THAT NEEDS NO NEW AUTHORING. Seven sources already have both representations: Caston 1995, Frede 1992, Nussbaum 1985, O'Gorman 2005, Papachristou 2013 and White 1985 (corpus/index/Aristotelian Phantasia Secondary (1985-2017)) plus Bowin 2017 (corpus/index/Aristotelian Motion and Time Secondary), versus tmp/analysis-upgrade/production-sandbox/data/corpus/index/{caston-1995,frede-1992,nussbaum-1985,ogorman-2005,papachristou-2013,white-1985,bowin-2017}. Arm A = concept-level only; Arm B = same seven at claim level. 12 prompts x 2 arms x 3 seeds = 72 runs, roughly $22 at the sandbox's observed ~$0.30/run.

FIX THE RETRIEVAL CONTRACT BEFORE SCALING RECORDS. The caps are 12 ontology nodes / 3 hooks / 5 tensions (corpus-index-provider.ts:101-103) and 1 bridge (cross-author-utils.ts:498). Specify: two-stage retrieval (concepts select a candidate set, claims are retrieved within it, so claim count never competes with concept count); a per-source quota so a dense source cannot crowd out a sparse one; length-normalised scoring; and a claim budget additive to the concept budget. Gate on source-coverage retention >= baseline. The measured penalty for skipping this is quality 0.794 -> 0.789 with six named authors dropping out.

ADOPT THE PROVEN CLAIM SCHEMA AS THE UNION OF THE THREE THAT WORK. Required fields: claim_id (content-addressed), entry_id, source_id, unit_id, claim_text, quote_verbatim, span{doc_id, char_start, char_end, fulltext_sha256}, locus{edition, book_page, pdf_page, native{kind: bekker|H-page|section|timestamp|line_range, value}}, claim_type (closed enum), stance (closed enum), use_mention (closed enum), speaker, support_tier (closed enum), supports[], supported_by[], concept_ids[], faithfulness (closed enum), faithfulness_note, provenance. Derived from Dissertation phase2-claims.json (19 fields, 8-tier support taxonomy, supports/supported_by graph, line anchors), the sandbox claims.jsonl (Toulmin ground/warrant/qualifier/rebuttal + grounding.char_start/char_end + faithfulness), and Uexkull's Claim|Evidence type|Strength|Page ref.

REQUIRE A STORED FULLTEXT WITH A HASH, INSIDE THE REPO. Every span must reference {doc_id, fulltext_sha256}. In-Game's 995 line-range anchors died because /tmp/calleja-fulltext.txt was deleted (verified absent today). Specify a deterministic, re-runnable extraction command per source and store its output under version control or under a named durable path, never /tmp. A deterministic re-extraction resurrects roughly 1,000 clause pointers in one step.

PUBLISH EVERY CLOSED VOCABULARY IN THE PLAN AS A LITERAL LIST. At minimum: relation, edge_domain, claim_type, stance, use_mention, support_tier, faithfulness, centrality_tier, tag/confidence. Enforce at validation with a named failure. Evidence of need: 15 uncontrolled claim_type values in the sandbox, 162 uncontrolled stance values with 195 nulls in Boredom Secondary, ~36 type values corpus-wide, 12 centralityTier shapes including 4 blobs up to 10,009 characters.

ONE CANONICAL EDGE RECORD, ZERO NEW DIALECTS. {edge_id, entry_id, source_id, relation, target_id, domain, evidence_locus, provenance, note}. Enumerate all 47 observed edge-CSV headers in the plan as a one-time migration table -- the migration spec's '>=10 header layouts' (:61) understates by ~4.7x. Reject any file whose header is not byte-identical to canonical after BOM/CRLF normalisation, and name the offending file.

ONE TENSION SHAPE COVERING ALL EIGHT ON DISK. {tension_id, entry_id, endpoint_a{node_id,label}, endpoint_b{node_id,label}, relation, directed, evidence_locus_a, evidence_locus_b, description, unit_ids[]}. Must subsume node_a/node_b/dependency_edge/conflict_edge, nodeA/nodeB/type, wendt_position/against, pole_A/pole_B, tension_id/label/supporting_units, tension_id/label/pentad_terms_involved + unmatched_raw_tensions, and the FCM locus_a/locus_b variant. The migration spec's superset (:73-81) covers 1 of the 4 currently-broken shapes.

BRIDGES REQUIRE TWO RESOLVED ENDPOINTS OR THEY DO NOT EXIST. Required: {bridge_id, source_entry_id, source_node_id, target_entry_id, target_node_id, bridge_text (min length), evidence_locus_source, evidence_locus_target, state: proposed|evidence-attached|confirmed}. Empty endpoint = hard validation failure. Endpoints must resolve to registered node ids, not free-text names. Reject any parsed value still containing '[INTERP-'. This single gate would have prevented 42 broken hooks and the 525 wasted bridge candidates anchored on them.

GATE ANCHOR VALIDITY BEFORE ANY DERIVATIVE GENERATION. Measured cost of not doing so: 525 of 552 sandbox bridge candidates (95%) were generated against an empty-target anchor, of which 465 came back 'unrelated'; the 27 generated against well-formed anchors returned 25 usable (93%). A 6x yield difference. Require: anchor-validity rate = 1.00 before generation, plus an anchor-coverage metric, since only 8 of 72 hooks were ever exercised.

THE BRIDGE SELECTOR MUST REJECT EMPTY ENDPOINTS BEFORE SCORING, AND OMIT THE BLOCK WHEN NOTHING SCORES. cross-author-utils.ts:473-474 lets t.includes('') match everything; computeMatchScore (:424) guards empties but the filter does not. Simulated over 6 realistic dissertation topics, 4 of 6 select an empty-target hook as MANDATORY. Specify: filter empties first; if no candidate scores > 0, emit no MANDATORY block rather than degrading to '?' (gold-standard-prompt-builder.ts:712-713); never label an INTERP-tagged record 'verified' (:710-711).

STRUCTURED LOCUS, NEVER OPAQUE. Reverse migration-spec :56 ('triple-pagination -> one opaque composite locus (don't parse)'). Name and store each subfield separately with an edition tag. Being and Time's triple pagination is an asset, not noise.

PAGE-OFFSET PROBE AS A BLOCKING PER-SOURCE GATE. Sample K >= 5 loci spread across the document, extract text at the declared offset, assert token match against the recorded quote or heading, write results to the entry's gates.json. Treat a non-constant offset as a hard failure requiring a per-range offset table, not a scalar. Evidence: Aristotle 33/34 records wrong by up to 47 pages; bekker-index 101/188 loci off by >2; Rickert declared 20, actual drifts 18 -> 15.

MACHINE-READABLE gates.json PER ENTRY, MANDATORY. Only 2 of 27 entries have any quality report and only 1 has metrics. Contents: schema validation result, record counts by type (declared vs actual), span coverage %, locator probe results, id uniqueness, referential integrity, enum conformance, reachability (records reaching runtime), and the anchor-validity rate.

MANIFEST AS CONTRACT, NOT DESCRIPTION. Declare expected counts per record type BEFORE authoring; validator computes actuals; mismatch blocks registration. Dissertation phase2-claims.json already demonstrates it (claim_count_target '140-180', claim_count_actual 156). Count-mismatch is the largest defect class at 66 of 551.

GATES THAT ARE NON-VACUOUS AT N=1. Write per-entry gates first and make corpus-level checks a rollup. At N=1 every gate in the migration spec's Section 8 (census, adapter coverage, 4-shape superset, parity diff) evaluates to nothing. Non-vacuous at N=1: schema validation; every quoted claim resolves to a span; density within a declared band; zero dangling refs; zero duplicate ids; locus probe passes; entry appears in the reachability report with >0 records.

CLAIM DENSITY TARGET PER SOURCE, DECLARED AND MEASURED. Evidence for a workable band: Dissertation achieves one record per ~58 words; Veri(dis)similitude 262 addressable rows / 15,481 words = one per 59 words; the sandbox achieves 155-512 claims per article. Concept-level entries achieve ~5 readings per article. State the target as records-per-1000-words with a floor, and record actual.

AUTO-DISCOVERY PLUS entry.json, NOT A HARDCODED REGISTRY. Replace compile-corpus-index.py TEXT_DIRS (:34-129, 19 hardcoded dirs against 27 on disk) with directory walk plus a per-entry entry.json declaring {entry_id, adapter, schema_version, expected_record_counts}. Registration must be impossible to forget.

EVERY AUTHORED ARTIFACT TYPE MUST NAME ITS CONSUMER (file:function). Any type with no named consumer is not authored. Today 19,989 edge rows exist and grep -c 'edges.csv' scripts/compile-corpus-index.py = 0. Also resolve the .md-vs-.json twin problem: the compiler reads book-level-ontology.md (:1199, :1221) and never the .json, which cost In-Game and Uncomfortable 18 canonical positions each.
EMBED AT CLAIM GRANULARITY FROM V1, concept vectors derived as centroids. Reverse migration-spec :110. One vector per concept reproduces the ceiling in the vector layer.

SPAN COVERAGE IS A GATE WITH A FLOOR, NOT A TOLERANCE. Reverse migration-spec :118 ('downstream checks must tolerate locus-only concepts'). The sandbox already achieves 93.0% (4,615 of 4,961); set the floor at 90% and quarantine the rest with a report. Add a match_ratio floor (the sandbox's minimum is 0.083 while its median is 1.000) so 'grounded' is not satisfiable by a near-random match.

CONTENT-ADDRESSED IDS, NEVER POSITIONAL. entry_id + unit_id + sha256(claim_text)[0:8]. Reverse migration-spec :64's '{unit}-c{n}'. Positional ids renumber on every insert and are the mechanism behind 44 dangling-reference and 10 id-collision defects.

CANONICAL-TERM ADMISSION GATE. A term enters the global greedy-match list only if it is declared in a per-entry terms file, exceeds a minimum length, and is not a bare common English word. Measured pollution today: canonicalTerms holds 1,722 entries including whole sentences ('Debate axis 9: social presence reliably predicts satisfaction/learning <-> effects inconsistent/assumed-not-demonstrated') and the bare words 'technological', 'Presence' and 'control', all matching corpus-wide.
STAMP schema_version INTO EVERY ARTIFACT. Only Dissertation does it today ('DISSERTATION-ANALYSIS-PIPELINE-PLAN-v1.4-8.1.1'). Without it no future migration can know what shape a file is.

PROMOTE THE 4,961 EXISTING SPAN-ANCHORED CLAIMS OUT OF tmp/. They cover 24 sources, 93.0% carry char spans, and 14,811 concept-mentions already link them to ontology nodes with provenance{bekker, chunk_id, char_start, char_end} -- the wiring from claim level up to the existing concept graph. Migrate into corpus/index/_atoms/<source-slug>/ under the new schema. This is the single largest available jump toward the goal and requires re-authoring nothing. Forbid new index artifacts under tmp/.

SHIP A QUERY SURFACE AS A NAMED DELIVERABLE WITH ACCEPTANCE TESTS: given a topic, return top-k claim records with spans, concept ids and source. An index nobody can query cannot improve drafting. Confirmed gap: zero references to claims.jsonl / concept-mentions.jsonl / bridge-candidates across src/ and scripts/.

RESOLVE THE VERBATIM-SUPPRESSION POLICY EXPLICITLY. In-Game ig-10-deep.json:434-441 and Uncomfortable us-03-radcliffe.json:110,:234 deliberately suppress quoted text. A clause-level index needs the clause. Either exempt index-internal storage from the policy with an access rule, or accept that those two entries cannot reach clause level and say so.

EVERY PHASE MUST END WITH RECORDS REACHING RUNTIME, AND THAT NUMBER MUST STRICTLY INCREASE. Reverse the migration spec's all-or-nothing cutover (:17, :138, :140). Land the new record types alongside the existing compiled index in the current runtime before any storage migration.

NO OPEN ITEMS WITHOUT AN OWNER, A METHOD, A DEADLINE PHASE AND A DEFAULT DECISION. The comparison report's five open items (:65-72) propagated unchanged into the migration spec (:148) and blocked nothing while resolving nothing; the A/B/C plan's five open questions (:232-238) contributed to the experiment never running.

PIN THE EXPERIMENT CONFIG IN VERSION CONTROL WITH A RECORDED SHA -- prompt list, source list, seed list, arm definitions -- exactly as ARTIFACT-MANIFEST.json does for canonical-suite.json ('FROZEN -- must not be modified without incrementing version and recording new SHA').

BUDGET AND COST MODEL STATED UP FRONT. Observed reference points: $20 to extract 3,776 claims from 15 papers (~$1.33/paper, ~$0.005/claim); $1.80 for 6 prose-validation runs (~$0.30/run); $26.60 for the whole session. A 27-entry claim-level pass at that rate is on the order of $40-80 for extraction plus harness runs -- state it so the programme is not scoped by guesswork.

SINGLE-RUN-OF-RECORD RULE. corpus/index/Dissertation carries two identical full run-histories (2026-05-13T1439 and 2026-05-20T0058). Keep the immutable-run plus living-pointer pattern (_living/latest.md is good) but state which run counts for metrics, so counts are not doubled.
what_to_preserve: Import from per-entry SOURCE files, never from compiled-index.json (migration spec :14-17). The lossiness is precisely documented and verified today: compile-corpus-index.py has zero references to edges.csv, reads book-level-ontology.md and never the .json twin (:1199, :1221), and globs cross-pipeline hooks only from the Aristotle directory (:1244).

The adversarial-correction discipline itself. The comparison report's Section 5 (:57-62) reverses an earlier wrong claim ('the compiler never reads tensions') while keeping the conclusion, and re-verifies against real source. Keep the pattern of stating what was checked, against which file and line, and what changed.

Naming adapter coverage rather than substrate as the long pole (migration spec :15, :133, :142). Correct diagnosis; the new plan should keep it and extend it from 19 entries to 27 and from 10 CSV dialects to 47.

The CSV header-sniffing dialect normalizer as a mandatory pre-insert layer (migration spec :61), with the explicit warning that a fixed positional reader corrupts data. Keep it; widen its scope and make it permanent rather than migration-only.

The scorer correction (migration spec :91): scoreCandidate uses JS .match(), i.e. substring counting anywhere in searchText, so 'design' counts inside 'designer'. Verified at corpus-index-provider.ts:81-91. Any reimplementation using token equality silently diverges. Keep this, and keep the warning that three distinct scorers with different thresholds must stay separate (:100).

Corpus-FIRST retrieval policy: the authored ontology always runs and seeds query expansion; vectors are additive, never a substitute (migration spec :89, comparison report :28). Keep the policy, change only the granularity of what the ontology query returns.
New corpus_* relations strictly additive, never touching kb_* (migration spec :11). Sound isolation.
Deterministic content-hash ids and idempotent, re-runnable import (migration spec :17). Keep and extend to authoring-time id assignment.

The A/B/C process firewall (eval plan :89-95): draft fully in one condition before opening the other index. This is the plan's best methodological feature and the new plan should keep it for any human-in-the-loop arm.
Pre-registering hypotheses before running (eval plan :174-201). Keep the practice; replace the specific hypotheses with measurable ones.

The three-way rather than two-way design (eval plan :21-26): what each index yields alone, what fusion uniquely enables, and the deltas. The insight that a binary comparison penalises each index for not doing what it was not designed for is correct and worth keeping.

H6 (eval plan :198-200): feed atomic claims into the narrative pipeline, with the synthesiser pointing at specific high-faithfulness claims rather than at page citations -- 'prose hierarchy on top, atomic provenance underneath, with programmatic verifiability of every assertion'. This is exactly the target architecture and it was written down 15 months ago. Keep it and build it.

The reframing of the atom index's design intent as cross-author conceptual matching on a shared ontology, made trustworthy by grounding plus faithfulness (eval plan :30-38). Correct, and the artifact bears it out: 14,811 concept-mentions each carrying ontology_node plus provenance{bekker, chunk_id, char_start, char_end}.
The SHA-frozen prompt suite pattern (ARTIFACT-MANIFEST.json canonical_prompt_suite: 'FROZEN -- must not be modified without incrementing version and recording new SHA'). Reuse verbatim.

The release/activate artifact-versioning pattern in the sandbox (create-release.sh / activate-release.sh, ARTIFACT-MANIFEST.json with per-artifact current_version plus symlink). It is the only place in the repo where index artifacts are versioned and swappable.
The Dissertation entry's contract-manifest pattern: claim_count_target vs claim_count_actual, support_tier_distribution, and schema_version stamped into the artifact. Generalise it to every entry.
The immutable _run-history/<timestamp>/ plus _living/latest.md pattern in corpus/index/Dissertation. Good reproducibility shape; add a single-run-of-record rule so counts are not doubled.

Keeping the existing pipeline live with rollback until a replacement is validated (migration spec :17, comparison report :87). Keep the safety property; drop the all-or-nothing cutover that delays all value to the final phase.

The usage plan's cross-pipeline hook CONCEPT -- that inter-author connections should be pre-mapped so a writer does not rediscover them (:82, :324-328). The idea is right; only the schema, the coverage and the verification were missing.

The usage plan's anti-hallucination flag stack as a baseline configuration (:275-282), particularly --whitelist, --citation-max-hallucinations 0 and --citation-enforcement-mode strict. Keep it as the fixed configuration for every harness arm so the arms differ only in the index.

scope: plans/secondary-cluster-index-plan-TEMPLATE-2026-07-15.md (238 lines, read in full) and its named structural precedent plans/boredom-secondary-cluster-index-plan-2026-07-14.md (288 lines, read in full). Traced every mandated artifact and every §8 gate against ground truth: scripts/compile-corpus-index.py (1,412 lines, read in relevant part), scripts/normalize-edges.py:267-274, corpus/index/compiled-index.json (701 nodes / 64 tensionEdges / 1,722 canonicalTerms), and the template-built and precedent entries on disk — Boredom Secondary (Part III), VR Pedagogy Secondary (Part III), Red Dead Redemption 2 Secondary (2019-2023), Aristotelian Phantasia Secondary (1985-2017), In-Game (Calleja 2011), Uncomfortable Situations, Wendt - Design for Dasein, A Grammar of Motives (Burke 1945), Von Uexkull, Veri(dis)similitude (Salvo MA). All measurements below were recomputed directly from the filesystem, not taken from the audit summary.
summary: The template is a well-engineered plan for producing a scholarly reading-apparatus and a badly engineered plan for producing an index. Its central, fatal property: it mandates roughly 14 synthesis artifacts plus three files per source — and the compiler reads exactly ONE of them. Of 1,759 files / 35.3 MB under corpus/index, the compiled runtime artifact is 664 KB containing name-only nodes with no ids, no page numbers, no quotes, and no loci. Boredom Secondary's 55 unit JSONs (2,588 sub-items with page loci and provenance tags), 1,897 global edges, 72 lemmas, 12 debate axes and its whole construct x measure concordance reach runtime as 61 bare concept names.
